content.overview: Hindu marriage is governed primarily by the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. Core modules: conditions of a valid marriage (s. 5); restitution of conjugal rights (s. 9); void marriages (s. 11); voidable marriages (s. 12); divorce (s. 13); divorce by mutual consent (s. 13B); interim maintenance (s. 24); permanent alimony (s. 25).
content.glance: Route by issue: validity → s. 5/11/12; restitution → s. 9; divorce → s. 13/13B; maintenance → s. 24/25.
content.study:
Use this overview to route fact patterns to section-specific topics. Do not treat the overview as a substitute for those notes.

No case holdings invented. Case-law verification remains a separate gate.

sections.heading: Conditions — s. 5
sections.body: Monogamy, mental capacity, age, prohibited degrees, sapinda (subject to custom).

sections.heading: Void and voidable — ss. 11–12
sections.body: Void: bigamy, prohibited degrees, sapinda. Voidable: incapacity, consent vitiated, pregnancy by another, etc.

sections.heading: Restitution — s. 9
sections.body: Decree for restitution of conjugal rights when one spouse withdraws without reasonable excuse.

sections.heading: Divorce — ss. 13, 13B
sections.body: Fault and other grounds under s. 13; mutual consent under s. 13B.

examples.title: Routing
examples.body: Petition for divorce on cruelty — open s. 13 topic; interim support — open s. 24.

hypotheticals.question: Where do you start a Hindu marriage problem?
hypotheticals.analysis: Identify the remedy sought (validity, restitution, divorce, maintenance) and open the matching section topic.

distinctions.title: Void (s. 11) vs voidable (s. 12)
distinctions.left: Null from the start; decree of nullity.
distinctions.right: Valid until avoided; petition by aggrieved spouse.

misconceptions.trap: One section decides every Hindu marriage dispute.
